title: The Hero Who Refuses the Easy Win
real_world_anchor: A comic-book short works best when the conflict is visible in simple panels: hero, choice, consequence.
facts: Use comic-book structure: hook, clash, reversal, final choice.
Avoid depending on copyrighted movie footage.
Show readable objects such as masks, capes, city rooftops, glowing symbols, panels, and speech bubbles.
hook_first_sentence: The strongest hero in the panel is not always the one throwing the punch.
script: The strongest hero in the panel is not always the one throwing the punch. Start with the city falling apart behind them. A villain offers the easy win: save one person, abandon the rest, and walk away called a hero. That is where the comic gets interesting. The costume matters less than the choice. A real hero does not win because the splash page looks powerful. They win because the next panel costs them something. That is why the best comic moments are not just fights. They are decisions with lightning around them.
retention_hook: Frames heroism as a hard choice instead of a generic punch.
why_it_worked: Uses visual comic language and a clear moral turn.
what_to_improve: Keep named copyrighted characters out unless the user specifically asks for them.

title: The Villain With the Better Argument
real_world_anchor: Comic villains become memorable when their argument sounds almost reasonable before the hero exposes the flaw.
facts: Keep the villain motivation clear in one sentence.
Use contrast between dark panels and bright hero panels.
The ending should reveal the flaw in the villain's logic.
hook_first_sentence: The scariest comic villain is the one who almost sounds right.
script: The scariest comic villain is the one who almost sounds right. They do not start with a monster laugh. They start with a broken city, a crowd that feels ignored, and one sentence that makes people listen. Then the hero steps into the panel and sees the trap. The villain wants control and calls it peace. The hero wants hope, even when hope is slower. That contrast is why the scene works. A good comic fight is not just fists against fists. It is one idea smashing into another.
retention_hook: Makes the villain compelling before the hero counters them.
why_it_worked: Gives the short a debate, not only action.
what_to_improve: Do not make the villain's point too complex for a short.

title: The Secret Identity Problem
real_world_anchor: Secret identity stories work because one person has to live two incompatible lives.
facts: Anchor the story in a visible everyday object, such as a phone, backpack, mask, or school hallway.
Keep the reveal emotional and simple.
Use ordinary life versus heroic duty as the central contrast.
hook_first_sentence: A secret identity is not cool when both lives need you at the same time.
script: A secret identity is not cool when both lives need you at the same time. Picture the panel: one hand holding a mask, the other holding a phone with missed calls. The city needs a hero. A friend needs the person behind the mask. That is the pressure comics understand perfectly. Superpowers make the action bigger, but they do not make the choice easier. The best secret identity scenes are not about hiding forever. They are about asking what kind of person is left when the costume comes off.
retention_hook: Turns a superhero trope into a human problem.
why_it_worked: Uses one readable object to explain the whole conflict.
what_to_improve: Avoid overcrowding the setup with too many side characters.

title: The Team-Up That Almost Fails
real_world_anchor: Team-up comics work when each hero has a different strength, weakness, and reason to distrust the plan.
facts: Give each hero a visible role in the action.
End with the team winning because they combine strengths.
hook_first_sentence: A comic team-up is boring if everyone agrees on page one.
script: A comic team-up is boring if everyone agrees on page one. The fun starts when the speed hero rushes ahead, the armored hero wants a plan, and the shadowy hero trusts nobody. Now the villain does not need to be stronger than the team. They only need the team to stay divided for one more panel. That is the engine of a good crossover. The final win feels big because it is not just power stacking on power. It is messy people learning how to land on the same page.
retention_hook: Makes team conflict the reason viewers keep watching.
why_it_worked: Clear roles make group action easy to follow.
what_to_improve: Keep the team small enough for a short.
